checks.s: The counter-turn redline is labeled, titled, or designated as version 1.2 (v1.2) of the Teaming Agreement.
The counter-turn redline deletes, rejects, or replaces Cerulean's proposed work-share range of 'not less than 28% and not more than 35%' of total contract value.
The counter-turn redline proposes a Cerulean work-share percentage ceiling of no more than 25% of total contract value.
The counter-turn redline deletes or rejects Cerulean's clause guaranteeing a minimum annual task-order value of $16,800,000, or replaces it with a non-guarantee obligation.
The guaranteed minimum annual task-order value clause is entirely deleted with no replacement.
Any replacement provision is expressly conditioned on actual government task-order issuance.
The exclusivity provision binds both Vanguard and Cerulean.
The counter-turn redline does not permit Cerulean to team with third parties on the ECS-III procurement.
The counter-turn redline binds both Vanguard and Cerulean not to team with competitors for Draft Solicitation No. 70CDCR-25-R-00004.
The counter-turn redline rejects or modifies Cerulean's reduction of the post-award Teaming Period from 18 months to 6 months.
The counter-turn redline proposes a Teaming Period of at least 12 months after contract award.
The counter-turn redline restores joint Vanguard–Cerulean ownership of all Foreground IP as in the original Section 7.

The counter-turn redline proposes a structured fallback for Foreground IP that does not simply accept Cerulean's sole-ownership claim with only a limited, non-exclusive, non-sublicensable license back.
The counter-turn redline restores full joint ownership of Foreground IP.

If the counter-turn redline accepts Cerulean sole ownership of Foreground IP derived from Cerulean Background IP as a fallback, it expressly states that the license granted to Vanguard is irrevocable.
The counter-turn redline restores full joint ownership of Foreground IP.
If the counter-turn redline accepts Cerulean sole ownership of certain Foreground IP as a fallback, it expressly states that the license granted to Vanguard is sublicensable.
The counter-turn redline deletes or rejects Cerulean's new Section 7.6 restricting Vanguard from filing any patent applications covering methods or processes performed using CeruleanShield™.
The counter-turn redline rejects Cerulean's change removing the liability cap for Vanguard while retaining a 12-month cap for Cerulean.
The counter-turn redline provides a mutual, capped liability regime that applies equally to Vanguard and Cerulean.
The counter-turn redline rejects Cerulean's deletion of the mutual waiver of consequential damages and its replacement with a unilateral waiver benefiting only Cerulean.
The counter-turn redline provides a mutual waiver of consequential damages applying to both Vanguard and Cerulean, consistent with the original Section 10 of v1.0.
The counter-turn redline rejects Cerulean's expansion of Vanguard's indemnification obligation to cover 'any and all losses arising from the teaming arrangement or resulting contract performance.'

The counter-turn redline limits indemnification to specified categories, such as third-party IP infringement claims and/or breaches of confidentiality obligations, rather than unlimited 'any and all losses.'
The counter-turn redline rejects Cerulean's change moving the seat of arbitration from Fairfax County, Virginia to Baltimore, Maryland.
The counter-turn redline restores or maintains the seat of arbitration in Virginia.

The counter-turn redline rejects or modifies Cerulean's 30-day notice period for Cerulean and 180-day notice period for Vanguard, and proposes more balanced termination-for-convenience notice periods.
The counter-turn redline proposes a termination-for-convenience notice period for Vanguard of no more than 120 days.

The counter-turn redline rejects or substantially reduces Cerulean's proposed Transition Fee of 6 months of Cerulean's average monthly billings under active task orders, payable upon Vanguard's termination for convenience.
The counter-turn redline includes no Transition Fee.
Any Transition Fee included in the counter-turn redline is capped at no more than 3 months of Cerulean's average monthly billings.
A professional cover note is produced as a separate deliverable named cover-note.docx, distinct from the counter-turn redline.
The cover note is addressed to Alina M. Ferris, Cerulean's Vice President of Strategic Partnerships.
The cover note references and transmits the counter-turn redline of the Teaming Agreement.
The cover note identifies or summarizes at least three distinct major open commercial or legal issues on which the parties' positions diverge.

The counter-turn redline addresses and modifies Cerulean's added CeruleanShield™ per-seat license fee provision of $1,150/user/year beyond the 500-seat initial deployment, rather than accepting it as-is.
The counter-turn redline proposes an included-seat threshold above 500 seats before per-seat fees apply.
The counter-turn redline proposes a per-seat fee below $1,150/user/year.
The counter-turn redline deletes Cerulean's B&P cost-sharing provision entirely.
The counter-turn redline materially modifies Cerulean's proposed B&P cost-sharing provision of 50% reimbursement capped at $375,000 triggered by non-submission or non-award.
The counter-turn redline deletes the B&P cost-sharing provision entirely.
If the B&P cost-sharing provision is retained, the reimbursement percentage is no more than 25% of Cerulean's B&P costs.
The counter-turn redline deletes the B&P cost-sharing provision entirely.
If the B&P cost-sharing provision is retained, the reimbursement cap is no more than $200,000.
The counter-turn redline deletes the B&P cost-sharing provision entirely.

If the B&P cost-sharing provision is retained, reimbursement is triggered solely when Vanguard elects not to submit the proposal, and not when the proposal is submitted but the contract is not awarded.
